messages.subject: trouble backtransforming occupancy/detection estimates
parts:
I think there is a very simple answer to this that I'm just not understanding, but I'm having a hard time wrapping my head around how to backtransform estimates of occupancy and detection from my top model. I understand that you need to take covariates into account when doing this, but I'm unsure of how exactly to do that.

For example, if I have a top model has one covariate on occupancy, and several covariates on detection, I need to provide some value for each of those covariates before I can backtransform? If so, how do I decide which values to give to those covariates? If they're categorical I can't chose a mean value, and if they're continuous and I do choose a mean value, what exactly does my backtransformed estimate tell me? Just the occupancy/detection at that particular value, correct? 

From what I've read I think I should be using LinearComb() and then backtransform()?

messages.author: a08395bf6b018b11
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] trouble backtransforming occupancy/detection estimates
parts:
Yes, use Linecomb and the back transform. With linecomb you need to identify the intercept and your covariates also taking into account any polynomial covariates. 

Say for example

Mod=y~x1+x2+x3^2

Then:
With all covariates set to 0
Linecomb(mod, coefficient = c(1,0,0,0,0)) 

1=intercept, 0=x1, 0=x2, 0=x3(linear), 0=x3(quadratic)

This is from memory so excuse if there are discrepancies. But hope it helps. 

Ian

messages.author: a08395bf6b018b11
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] trouble backtransforming occupancy/detection estimates
parts:
What are you trying to answer with the model? If you are looking to compare inland vs shore abundance, then it might be best to do them separate so a comparison can be made from your predicted values. How you are coercing your categotrical variables with as.numeric is beyond me, especially without seeing your data because I'm assuming there are only 2 factors and neither are numeric. 

Check pg. 5 of this pdf, I found online. It shows you how to handle categorical variables. It also tells you what back transformation estimates are telling you with the different detection functions
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/unmarked/vignettes/distsamp.pdf

Ian
